SMTO-FIL-0004 — SMTO tried to read a non-text file as text

GUID: c7be0beb-151a-4a57-9605-f3c7d7e887da
Slug: file-binary-file
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • The file looks like a picture, archive, program or other non-text file, so SMTO couldn't open it as text. The file was not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check what kind of file it is, for example a PDF, image, zip archive or program. Only plain-text files can be read or edited line by line.
  2. Ask SMTO to handle it as raw data instead of text, for example to copy it, report its size, or convert it with a suitable tool. SMTO can work with non-text files as raw data without trying to read them as words.
  3. If you're sure it is a text file, tell SMTO which text encoding it uses, such as UTF-16. Some text formats look like non-text unless SMTO knows how they were saved.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads or handles the file without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's name and type, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Text inspection rejected the file as binary because of a known binary signature (PNG, JPEG, ZIP, ELF, gzip) or NUL bytes outside UTF-16 content.

What this means

  • Text inspection detected NUL characters outside the supported UTF-16 handling and classified the content as binary. Why this can happen

  • Text inspection detected NUL characters outside the supported UTF-16 handling and classified the content as binary.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect encoding/BOM and the intended representation; NUL detection is a format check, not a complete file-type classifier.

How to fix it

  • Read the file with mode=bytes or a format-specific tool instead of a text operation. If the content is really UTF-16 text, request utf-16-le or utf-16-be, or generic utf-16 only when the file starts with a UTF-16 byte-order mark.
  • Use a bytes-capable operation instead of a text operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported bytes operation or correctly identified text encoding reads the intended content.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.
